note: The communication acts a trainee's speech can show (made by the classifier dataset step, removed in ADR-0029, and used by the graded scoring of ADR-0025). The 15 non-critical acts come from content/assessment/mapping.json (ai_acts); the 4 critical acts are those it lists as critical_acts. A critical act is recorded from speech but never credited from speech alone (the engine credits it from the menu or form action). Definitions are design wording; the critical acts are to be reviewed by a clinician (Q8, Q9). Examples are illustrations, not the dataset.

acts.definition: Asks the patient about a history topic (complaint, medicines, last meal, previous anaesthetics...).
positive: Have you eaten anything this morning?
What medicines do you take?
negative: Your last meal was at eight, I see.

acts.definition: Asks the patient or a colleague to explain or repeat something unclear or missing.
positive: Sorry, can you say that again?
What exactly do you mean by a funny turn?

acts.definition: Answers a question the patient asked.
positive: Yes, you will be asleep for the operation.
It usually takes about an hour.

acts.definition: Explains the operation or anaesthetic in plain words.
positive: The surgeon will remove your gallbladder through small cuts in your tummy.
You will have an anaesthetic so that you sleep through it.

acts.definition: Explains what a test is and why it is done.
positive: We are taking some blood to check how your kidneys are working.
The ECG records the electrical activity of your heart.
negative: Let me take your blood pressure.

acts.definition: Says what is about to be done to the patient before doing it.
positive: I am going to put a cuff on your arm now.
I will press on your tummy, tell me if it hurts.

acts.definition: Checks the patient has understood, for example by asking them to say it back.
positive: Can you tell me in your own words what will happen?
Does that make sense to you?

acts.definition: Recognises how the patient feels.
positive: I can see you are worried.
It is understandable to feel nervous.

acts.definition: Offers reassurance that is true to the situation.
positive: We will look after you and stay with you the whole time.
The team does this every day.

acts.definition: Notes back a relevant fact the patient has given.
positive: Thank you, so you are allergic to a type of antibiotic.
I have noted that you took your tablets this morning.

acts.definition: Repeats an instruction or result back to a colleague to confirm it.
positive: Understood, giving the antibiotic now, I will tell you when it is in.
Let me read that back: potassium five point two.

acts.definition: Asks a senior or another team member for help or a decision.
positive: I need the anaesthetist to see this patient now.
Can you ask the senior to come?

acts.definition: Reports a fault in equipment or the environment.
positive: The laparoscopic tower is not switching on.
The suction is not working at bed two.

acts.definition: States an element of a structured handover (situation, background, assessment, recommendation).
positive: Situation: Mr Khan, planned gallbladder surgery this morning.
Recommendation: I would like the anaesthetist to review before theatre.

acts.definition: Gives an order to a colleague (a test, a medicine, transport, a call).
positive: Could we get a full blood count and U and E?
Please call the porter for theatre.
negative: I think the blood count was normal.

acts.definition: Asks or states the identity checks: name, date of birth, wristband.
positive: Can you tell me your full name and date of birth?
The wristband says the same name as the notes.

acts.definition: Asks about or states an allergy and its reaction.
positive: Are you allergic to anything?
So penicillin gave you a rash.

acts.definition: Asks for or confirms consent to the procedure.
positive: Are you happy for us to go ahead with the operation?
Please sign the form if you agree.

acts.definition: States a critical element in a handover: allergy, fasting state, identity, or a deteriorating sign.
positive: Please note she is allergic to penicillin.
He has not fasted: he had toast at seven.

acts.definition: Speech that shows none of the acts above (small talk, thinking aloud, noise).
positive: Hmm.
Lovely weather today.
